problem_statement: There is no way to size a k_heap so that a requested allocation of N bytes reliably succeeds: a heap declared with N bytes has its usable capacity reduced by metadata (the heap header, bucket tables, the free list, the end marker and per-chunk headers), so small heaps can fail to allocate even a small fraction of their declared size. A helper should compute the minimum heap size required in order for an allocation of a given number of bytes to succeed, accounting for that metadata overhead, and the system heap should use it so that the configured memory pool can actually serve its advertised size.
twister_command: scripts/twister -p native_sim/native/64 -T tests/lib/heap -s tests/lib/heap/libraries.heap -s libraries.heap -O twister-out --no-clean -W
